topic: What if gravity were twice as strong? Everything would feel twice as heavy, and walking up stairs would be like carrying another person.

episode.title: What If Gravity Were Twice as Strong?

shots.narration: What if gravity were twice as strong?
shots.scene: Colourful 3D science lab, vertical frame, glowing Earth hologram above a projector, no text or symbols.
shots.action: Nova expands the Earth hologram before Byte.
shots.mood: Bright cyan glow, wide curious eyes, vivid purple accents.

shots.narration: Earth would pull everything downward twice as hard.
shots.scene: Colourful lab beside a glowing holographic Earth with a small ball above its surface, no text.
shots.action: Nova enlarges the downward light beams connecting the ball to Earth.
shots.mood: Clear blue holographic light, focused expressions, warm background.

shots.narration: [surprised] Everything would feel twice as heavy!
shots.scene: Lab demonstration platform beside an enlarged hologram of a ball resting on a spring, no markings.
shots.action: The holographic ball compresses the spring farther.
shots.mood: Bright orange spring, blue glow, Byte's wide luminous eyes.

shots.narration: Even standing would make your muscles work harder.
shots.scene: Colourful lab with a translucent holographic model of Nova beside the Earth display, no labels.
shots.action: Nova illuminates the standing model's leg muscles.
shots.mood: Warm coral muscle glow, attentive faces, clean bright lighting.

shots.narration: Stairs would feel like carrying another you.
shots.scene: Lab hologram showing Nova on a staircase with an equally sized translucent Nova-shaped load on her back, no text.
shots.action: The holographic Nova climbs a stair beneath the ghostlike load.
shots.mood: Playful purple hologram, exaggerated effort, cheerful golden lighting.

shots.narration: [excited] The same jump would take you less high.
shots.scene: Lab hologram of a soft exercise platform beneath a faint tall jump arc and a lower bright arc, no labels.
shots.action: A holographic Nova jumps along the lower arc.
shots.mood: Bouncy pose, sparkling cyan trail, bright lime accents.

shots.narration: Dropped objects would accelerate downward faster, too.
shots.scene: Colourful lab with a glowing holographic ball suspended over a padded demonstration tray, no text.
shots.action: Nova releases the holographic ball toward the tray.
shots.mood: Crisp blue motion trail, curious faces, soft amber lighting.

shots.narration: But stronger gravity wouldn't add any material to your body.
shots.scene: Lab beside a life-sized translucent Nova hologram containing a fixed cluster of glowing beads, no symbols.
shots.action: Nova sweeps a scanning light across the unchanged holographic body.
shots.mood: Calm turquoise glow, reassuring smile, jewel-coloured beads.

shots.narration: [surprised] Your mass stays unchanged; what if Earth stopped spinning?
shots.scene: Colourful lab with the unchanged body hologram beside a rotating holographic Earth, no text.
shots.action: Nova freezes the Earth hologram's rotation.
shots.mood: Bright planetary blues, Byte's astonished eyes, warm curious smiles.

episode.description: Dr. Nova shows Byte how stronger gravity would change everyday life, from climbing stairs to jumping. Discover why everything would feel twice as heavy—even though your mass would stay the same.
